content.text: I am labeling a fight 60. Round 1 ended with a corner swap span open event. I exited the labeling page. When I come back I cannot end that span. It just starts a new one without ending the one that started.
I'll look into how open corner_swap spans are tracked and resumed in the annotation UI, since this touches the in-flight label_events→fight_events migration.
Found it — this is a ref-based bug in [Annotate.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx:217). Let me check the actual data for fight 60 to see how many open spans exist before I fix the code.

content.text: The bug is confirmed: [Annotate.tsx:217](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx:217) tracks the open span id only in an in-memory `useRef`, which resets to `{}` on every mount. The span itself (id 4042, frame 9790, `end_frame=null`) is still sitting correctly in the DB — nothing is corrupted, the UI just "forgot" about it. I'll add a small effect to reseed that ref from the loaded data.

content.text:
Type-checks clean. Summary:

**Root cause**: [Annotate.tsx:217](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx:217)'s `openSpanRef` — which tracks the in-flight span id so a second `O`/`P` press knows what to close — lives only in memory. Leaving the page (or reloading) resets it to `{}`, even though the actual unclosed span is still sitting in the database with `end_frame=null`. So the next `O` press had no idea a span was already open and just created a new one.

**Data check**: fight 60's `corner_swap` spans in the DB are fine — only one open span exists (id 4042, frame 9790, `end_frame=null`), no duplicates were created, so nothing needs cleanup there.

**Fix**: added a `useEffect` in [Annotate.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx:217) that reseeds `openSpanRef` from the loaded `spans` data (any `corner_swap`/`excluded` span with `end_frame == null`) whenever it arrives, so returning to the page restores awareness of the open span.

Go back into fight 60's labeling page and press `O` at the point you want round 1's swap span to end — it should now close span 4042 instead of opening a new one.
